STEP 1 - Scene: A small snack or side plate with broccoli florets and a whole clementine/mandarin-type orange. Photographed from above, roughly top-down, on a white square plate sitting on a dark-edged counter or tray.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square white dish about 22-24 cm across its longest diagonal-free width; I take it as ~22 cm side-to-side. Area ≈ 22 x 20 cm of usable well ≈ 360 cm² (treating the well as roughly 20 cm usable width). The mandarin is about 5-6 cm across, which fits this scale.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Broccoli florets (about 4 pieces, total cluster roughly 7 x 5 cm)
- One whole orange/mandarin, about 5.5 cm diameter

STEP 4 - Area:
- Broccoli: ~8% of vessel area (≈29 cm²)
- Mandarin: ~5% of vessel area (≈18 cm²)
Food covers about 13% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Broccoli: 29 cm² x ~3 cm height (florets stacked) ≈ 87 ml
- Mandarin: sphere of 5.5 cm diameter ≈ 87 ml (volume of sphere ~ 4/3·π·2.75³ ≈ 87 ml)

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Broccoli: 87 ml x 0.5 g/ml ≈ 44 g. Florets are airy, so 0.5 is reasonable for cut vegetables.
- Mandarin: 87 ml x 0.7 ≈ 61 g (whole fruit is dense, close to its real mass of roughly 70-90 g; I use 75 g as a more realistic whole-fruit weight).

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Broccoli (cooked-ish, as plated): 44 g x 35 kcal/100 g ≈ 15 kcal
- Mandarin: 75 g x 47 kcal/100 g ≈ 35 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Four small broccoli florets plus one mandarin is a light snack. About 120 g total and ~50 kcal is plausible for what is visible and does not assume a larger serving.

Total: ~120 g, ~50 kcal.
